targetCoverage.title: Nonisotrivial elliptic families

source.match: Use the existing elliptic-scheme carrier; nonisotrivial means that j is nonconstant on the connected base.

proofRoute: Read the relative dimension-one comparison and the parent's fixed-pairing level interface; no replacement family record is introduced.
acceptance: A constant-j family does not meet the nonisotrivial hypothesis.

targetCoverage.title: Torsion local system and monodromy

source.match: The finite étale p-torsion is a rank-two F_p local system; an isomorphism retains its linear action.

proofRoute: Apply the scheme finite-cover/fibre-functor equivalence and its field comparison, transporting module structure and pairings.
acceptance: Projectivizing the representation discards quadratic characters and is insufficient for descent.

targetCoverage.title: Geometric Frey–Mazur for families

source.match: For N>0 there is M_N, uniform in algebraically closed characteristic-zero k and smooth connected U with gon(U)<N, such that actual p-torsion isomorphism of nonisotrivial elliptic schemes implies an isogeny over U for every prime p>M_N.

proofRoute: Use geometric rigidity, the Hecke lift with f[p]=λΨ, sign descent in the rank-one Hom lattice, and extension over U.
acceptance: The conclusion is over the original U, with no finite base cover in its place.

targetCoverage.title: Geometric Frey–Mazur over function fields

source.match: For K=k(B), with k algebraically closed of characteristic zero and B smooth proper of gonality <N, actual G_K-linear p-torsion isomorphism implies K-isogeny above the same uniform threshold.

proofRoute: Spread both curves and inverse torsion maps over a common good-reduction open, apply the family theorem, and take generic fibres; reverse using extension.
acceptance: Removing finitely many base points leaves the proper-model gonality unchanged.

targetCoverage.title: Gonality rigidity on the diagonal quotient

source.match: Every nonconstant bounded-gonality curve map to Z(p) has Hecke image for sufficiently large p, uniformly over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields.

proofRoute: Use the complex Hurwitz contradiction and the separate finite-type spreading node for arbitrary k.
acceptance: Both determinant components are included; N≤1 has no positive gonality <N.

targetCoverage.title: Diagonal quotient surface

source.match: Z(p) is the normal projective diagonal quotient of X(p)² by PGL₂(F_p), with two determinant-square-class components.

proofRoute: Descend composition of the two projective frames, and compare each component with the appropriate twisted fixed-pairing PSL₂ presentation.
acceptance: A nonsquare component must survive the comparison.

targetCoverage.title: Heegner CM points

source.match: CM⁺ consists of pairs with a common nonidentity projective stabilizer and equal compatible tangent characters.

proofRoute: Use the order-two/order-three effective cyclic stabilizers and prove independence of compatible lifts and generators.
acceptance: Equal j-invariants alone need not give a common stabilizer.

targetCoverage.title: Anti-Heegner CM points

source.match: CM⁻ uses the opposite compatible tangent character, and conjugating the second complex factor exchanges the two CM signs.

proofRoute: Use the same common-stabilizer carrier and transport the character comparison under conjugation.
acceptance: For the order-three lift the other eigenvalue is −1−t, rather than −t.

targetCoverage.title: Singular bicusps

source.match: A singular bicusp is a pair of cusps whose order-p projective stabilizers agree.

proofRoute: Identify nontrivial intersection of the order-p stabilizers with equality and transport the p-gon boundary under G.
acceptance: A pair with distinct cusp inertia groups is excluded.

targetCoverage.title: Compact triangle uniformization of X(p)

source.locator: BT16 opening of §3, pp.717–718; accepted replacement for Lemma 5, p.718
source.match: For prime p>5, a selected compact component is Ξ(p)\H for the (2,3,p) triangle quotient of PSL₂(Z), with effective deck group PSL₂(F_p).

proofRoute: Use the imported polygon/uniformization interface and distinguish cusp filling from the cusped cover; keep the surviving witness.
acceptance: The reciprocal-angle sum is hyperbolic at p=7 and not at p=5.

targetCoverage.title: Cusped systole asymptotic

source.match: Half the least cusped length among loops nontrivial after filling is 2 log p+O(1).

proofRoute: Use tr M≡2 mod p² for the lower bound and the accepted M_p for an upper bound that survives filling.
acceptance: The printed U(p)L(−p) witness dies after U^p is killed.

targetCoverage.title: Uniformizing triangle coordinates

source.match: The marked triangle has y_p=p/π+O(p⁻¹) and θ_p=π/3+O(p⁻¹); the owner's U_p,L_p fix this normalization.

proofRoute: Use the triangle cosine rule, determinant/order identities and the positive square-root branch.
acceptance: The square-root discriminant is positive at p=7 and negative at p=5.

targetCoverage.title: Separated cusp balls

source.match: Distinct cusps in the compact metric are separated by at least 2 log p−O(1), with radius log p−O(1) embedded cusp discs.

proofRoute: Use incident triangle stars before applying the global injectivity-radius theorem.
acceptance: The local cusp-star bound is established before the global radius, avoiding a circular proof.

targetCoverage.title: Comparison of compact and cusped metrics

source.match: For compact distance r to the nearest cusp, tanh²(r/2)h_Y≤h_X≤h_Y.

proofRoute: Apply Schwarz–Pick to the inclusion and to a cusp-free compact disc; take square roots when comparing lengths.
acceptance: On r≥R the length factor is coth(R/2), whereas quadratic forms use its square.

targetCoverage.title: Compact injectivity radius

source.match: The compact injectivity radius is 2 log p+O(1), with shortest nontrivial length 4 log p+O(1).

proofRoute: Combine the surviving upper witness with an excursion count, metric comparison and bounded detour for each deep cusp visit.
acceptance: Repeated visits to one cusp are counted; no at-most-one-cusp assertion is assumed.

targetCoverage.title: Cusp discs and radius comparison

source.match: The width-p coordinate q=exp(2πiz/p) identifies the embedded horoball disc with radius exp(−2πy/p) and yields both compact-radius containments.

proofRoute: Apply punctured-disc and filled-disc metric comparisons within the stated log p to 2 log p range.
acceptance: The factor p in the q-coordinate is retained.

targetCoverage.title: Hecke pullback of a cusp ball

source.match: For sufficiently large p and an integer m≥1 prime to p, assume log p+C<R and R+log m<2 log p−C, for a uniform constant C. Then the inverse cyclic Hecke image of a radius-R cusp ball lies in the union of balls of radius R+log m+C at the inverse cusps.

proofRoute: Use the branch imaginary-part factor between 1/m and m together with the two q-radius estimates.
acceptance: Both bounds log p+C<R and R+log m<2 log p−C are required; the upper bound alone does not justify the q-disc comparison. The parameter m is a positive integer prime to p.

targetCoverage.title: Integral matrix height

source.locator: §3.3 "Heights", Definition, p.721 (used on M₂(Z) in S′_δ, p.730)
source.match: The integral matrix height is the entrywise maximum norm, with h(AB)≤2h(A)h(B) and h(A⁻¹)=h(A) for SL₂.

proofRoute: Specialize the pinned entrywise norm and the two-term matrix product; no general height is newly defined.
acceptance: The two-by-two all-ones matrix requires the factor 2 in the product estimate.

targetCoverage.title: Short displacement at elliptic lifts

source.match: A component-preserving deck element moving a marked elliptic point less than δρ_X has an integral SL₂ lift of height O(p^(4δ)), for 0<δ<1/2.

proofRoute: Use compact/cusped comparison and the real and imaginary parts of Mi; repeat at the order-three vertex.
acceptance: A nonsquare component-switching PGL element is outside this lift statement.

targetCoverage.title: Short cusp displacement representatives

source.match: A cusp lift within (1+δ)ρ_X of the marked cusp lift is σγ_p(M)i y_p, with σ in the cusp stabilizer and h(M)=O(p^(4δ)).

proofRoute: Move an adjacent order-two vertex using the triangle star and apply the elliptic height bound.
acceptance: The stabilizer factor σ cannot be silently removed.

targetCoverage.title: Cusp double-coset height control

source.match: A short component-preserving cusp displacement lies in Hγ_p(M)H modulo Ξ, with the same height bound.

proofRoute: Lift a shortest path and retain the stabilizer choices at both ends.
acceptance: This is a double-coset assertion, rather than a single representative assertion.

targetCoverage.title: Unique nearby cusp lift

source.match: For sufficiently small fixed δ and large p, a distinct cusp has at most one lift in the radius-(1+δ)ρ_X ball about a chosen cusp lift.

proofRoute: The lower matrix entry is both divisible by p and O(p^(8δ)); choose 8δ<1 before taking p large.
acceptance: The printed δ<1/4 does not justify an O(p^(8δ)) quantity being <p.

targetCoverage.title: Intersection of cusp balls

source.match: Two radius-(1/2+δ)ρ_X balls about distinct cusps have intersection in a radius-δρ_X+O(1) ball.

proofRoute: Lift the lens using uniqueness, strengthen the smallness margin, and apply the hyperbolic midpoint-lens bound.
acceptance: The radius has a uniform additive constant and the centres are distinct.

targetCoverage.title: Counting nearby cusps

source.match: At any point there are O(p^(24δ)) cusps within (1/2+δ)ρ_X, for sufficiently small fixed δ.

proofRoute: Combine the lens with short integral matrix counting at a nearby elliptic vertex.
acceptance: A point near zero or one cusp satisfies the bound without a reconstruction premise.

targetCoverage.title: Corrected Heegner repulsion

source.locator: Erratum Proposition 2.1, p.2, replacing Proposition 14 pp.725–727
source.match: Two nearby distinct CM⁺ points of the same elliptic type lie on one cyclic T_m with m≤C_δp^(Aδ).

proofRoute: Use the corrected Heegner centralizer argument with h₀=1 and positive determinant in the definite algebra.
acceptance: The analogous ordinary-Hecke claim for CM⁻ is excluded.

targetCoverage.title: Centralizer rigidity at Heegner points

source.match: The two short-lift intertwining equations in the distinct-Heegner setup cut the matrix solution space to dimension at most one.

proofRoute: Use the Gaussian/Eisenstein centralizers; redundancy would force the integral determinant-one lifts to fix the elliptic vertex.
acceptance: For order three, det(aI+bt₀)=a²−ab+b².

targetCoverage.title: Conjugate Hecke loci

source.match: The conjugate Hecke locus is the second-factor conjugate of T_m, a real analytic locus in the original complex product.

proofRoute: Transport the metric and CM⁺ repulsion through the second-factor isometry, keeping the conjugate complex structure explicit.
acceptance: There is no algebraic divisor intersection C·T̄_m.

targetCoverage.title: Repulsion of singular bicusps

source.match: At least three nearby singular bicusps force all nearby ones onto one small ordinary or conjugate Hecke locus, with the strengthened tube/cusp-complement outputs.

proofRoute: Three projective-line incidence conditions give a unique small integral matrix; keep its determinant sign in the reconstruction.
acceptance: Two bicusps are insufficient, and multiplying a negative-determinant matrix by −1 does not make it positive.

targetCoverage.title: Big diagonals and small Hecke curves

source.match: Δ_g imposes both matched-coordinate equalities in S²; τ_(g,m) restricts its source to T_m, with a separate real analytic signed companion.

proofRoute: Use the diagonal action graph and midpoint argument for the max-product tube formula.
acceptance: The radius-R tube uses coordinate distances <2R, and Δ_g has codimension two.

targetCoverage.title: Diagonal-overlap dichotomy

source.match: More than C log p overlapping diagonal tubes force a bicusp configuration or proximity to an ordinary or conjugate small Hecke locus.

proofRoute: Separate cusp-normalizer and reduced-quadratic-centralizer cases; reconstruct signed matrices in the scalar-centralizer case.
acceptance: A conjugate small locus cannot be silently replaced by a holomorphic curve.

targetCoverage.title: Quantitative overlap near bicusps

source.match: The cusp rotation count is bounded by C min(p,1+p sinh R/sinh d) for d>0; at d=0 use p.

proofRoute: Use sinh(D/2)=sinh d times abs(sin(θ/2)) and count order-p rotation angles; use inverses for either projection.
acceptance: Keep the additive 1 and sinh R when R grows with log p.

targetCoverage.title: Small-height matrix reconstruction

source.match: A unique invertible projective solution of small integral linear equations has a primitive small integral lift Q with p∤det Q.

proofRoute: Use rank-three cofactors and lift small minors from mod p to Z; split the Smith-form interpretation according to the sign of det Q.
acceptance: Q and −Q have the same determinant sign; m is abs(det Q).

targetCoverage.title: Quadratic-torus height count

source.match: For a nonscalar reduced quadratic rational algebra, determinant-one integral centralizer elements of height ≤p^A number O_A(log p).

proofRoute: Bound imaginary/split unit groups directly and use uniform logarithmic separation of real quadratic units.
acceptance: A nonreduced unipotent algebra returns to the cusp branch; the logarithmic claim is not made there.

targetCoverage.title: Volume-to-degree decay

source.match: For fixed t>0, vol(C)/a(tρ_X)=O(p^(−2t)Deg C) uniformly in effective cycles.

proofRoute: Compose ρ_X=2 log p+O(1), a(r)=4πsinh²(r/2), and vol=2πDeg.
acceptance: The exponent is −2t and constant coordinate projections contribute degree zero.

targetCoverage.title: Heegner multiplicity decay

source.locator: Proposition 25 proof, pp.736–737, restricted by erratum §4.1
source.match: The CM⁺ multiplicity is O((p^(−2δ₂)+p^(3δ₁−1))Deg C) for a cycle without Hecke components.

proofRoute: Separate CM⁺ off/on small Hecke loci, use disjoint point balls off them and cyclic pull-push plus diagonal bounds on them.
acceptance: Choose 3δ₁<1 and then δ₂ sufficiently small before taking p large.

targetCoverage.title: Anti-Heegner multiplicity decay

source.match: The same decay holds for CM⁻, using conjugate Hecke tubes and no conjugate divisor intersection.

proofRoute: Use fixed ε-balls, holomorphic Hecke pull-push and the conjugate-diagonal relative volume estimate.
acceptance: The ratio is sinh ε/sinh R; its reciprocal would grow rather than decay.

targetCoverage.title: Total CM multiplicity decay

source.match: Total CM multiplicity is the sum of the separately proved positive and negative character bounds.

proofRoute: Use the CM partition and the minimum of their positive decay exponents.
acceptance: One cannot apply ordinary Heegner repulsion to both signs.

targetCoverage.title: Corrected singular-bicusp decay

source.locator: Proposition 26, p.737, with proof replaced by erratum Proposition 4.2 p.4
source.match: For every non-Hecke effective cycle, p times its SBC multiplicity is O(p^(−η)Deg C), with η>0.

proofRoute: Use the signed off/on small-Hecke split and the strengthened erratum argument on the diagonal and conjugate diagonal.
acceptance: An O(p^(−1+δ)) bound for mult_SBC is too weak for ramification.

targetCoverage.title: Bicusp error exponents

source.match: Choose δ₃ small first, then 3δ₁<2δ₃, then δ₂ small relative to δ₁; the two SBC exponents are −1−2δ₂ and −1−2δ₃+3δ₁.

proofRoute: Include both determinant signs and the cusp-ball overlap factor p^(24δ₃); fix δ₃ to absorb that factor before the remaining choices.
acceptance: For δ₃=1/1000, δ₁=1/10000, δ₂=1/100000, both p-weighted displayed exponents are negative; this tests signs, not all hidden geometric constants.

targetCoverage.title: Total big-diagonal multiplicity

source.match: Big-diagonal multiplicity decays for cycles outside every Δ_g whose two projected cycles are nonconstant and non-Hecke.

proofRoute: Apply the accepted overlap decomposition, signed tube estimates and separate point-ball comparison; the pencil construction supplies the extra hypotheses.
acceptance: The unrestricted printed proposition fails on curves inside T₁×T₁, where the accepted counterexample ratio is 3p/(p−6).

targetCoverage.title: Compact versus cusped curve volume

source.match: Define cusped area projectionwise; its positive difference from compact area on any measurable subset is O(p⁻¹vol C).

proofRoute: Integrate nonconstant projections and use the cusp/genus ratio; a constant cusp coordinate contributes zero.
acceptance: At p=7 the area ratio is 7, matching 1+6/(p−6), not an omitted cusp term.

targetCoverage.title: Hecke tube comparison and cusp exceptions

source.match: Away from suitably enlarged cusp balls, compact Hecke tubes compare with cusped ones; cusped Hecke branches are local isometries.

proofRoute: Apply holomorphic cyclic pull-push and the O(p⁻¹) total-measure error, then ordinary or conjugate relative tube bounds.
acceptance: The ordinary tube bound needs projected non-Hecke components; the conjugate bound is a volume statement.

targetCoverage.title: A gonality pencil gives a rational curve

source.match: A degree-n gonality pencil on the normalization of a curve birational to its image gives a nonconstant, generically injective P¹→SymⁿZ.

proofRoute: Use the relative finite-flat fibre-cycle map and disjoint images of distinct generic fibres.
acceptance: A ramified double-cover fibre is 2[f(b)], not its reduced support.

targetCoverage.title: Normalized pullback and quotient group

source.match: Normalizing a dominant component of the pullback of the pencil map gives C→Sⁿ and finite α:C→P¹, with stabilizer quotient C/H=P¹.

proofRoute: Use W=Gⁿ⋊S_n, generic orbit transitivity and the smooth proper curve/function-field dictionary; remove any action kernel for inertia.
acceptance: For n=1 the permutation factor vanishes but G-inertia remains.

targetCoverage.title: Projected cycles retain degrees

source.match: Weighted projected cycles are nonconstant and non-Hecke, with pair projections outside Δ_g; ΣDeg C_i=Deg C and Σ_(i<j)Deg C_ij=(n−1)Deg C.

proofRoute: Use transitivity on pencil slots, generic distinctness of fibres and the projection formula with generic map multiplicities.
acceptance: For n=1 the pair sum is empty; for n=2 each coordinate occurs once in it.

targetCoverage.title: Ramification support on four strata

source.match: Ramification support consists of CM⁺, CM⁻ or SBC in one slot, or simultaneous equalities Δ_g in two moved slots.

proofRoute: Separate stabilizers with trivial/nontrivial permutation; use étaleness on the free quotient locus and normalization branch inertia.
acceptance: A single matched X-coordinate equality does not define the required big-diagonal stratum.

targetCoverage.title: Stabilizer and ramification-index bounds

source.match: For fixed n and p>max(5,n), local effective cyclic inertia has order at most 6n!p, and at most 6n! off the SBC strata.

proofRoute: Raise an element to n! to remove permutation and use coordinate stabilizer orders dividing 2,3,p.
acceptance: Several bicusp slots still produce one factor p, rather than p^n.

targetCoverage.title: Ramification is negligible

source.match: Ram α is O_n(p^(−η_n)Deg C) uniformly in the pencil pullback.

proofRoute: Charge ramification to weighted projected multiplicities and combine the two CM, p-weighted SBC and qualified diagonal estimates.
acceptance: The degree identities absorb sums over slots and pairs without dropping map multiplicities.

targetCoverage.title: Contradictory Hurwitz bounds

source.match: Hurwitz gives 2g(C)−2=−2deg α+Ram α≤o(Deg C), while a largest nonconstant X-projection gives 2g(C)−2≥Deg C/(2n).

proofRoute: Use the algebraic canonical-degree convention and choose the uniform error coefficient <1/(2n).
acceptance: Retain −2deg α in the equality; there is no extra 2π in the algebraic lower bound.

targetCoverage.title: From local systems to a modular surface map

source.match: Actual finite étale torsion isomorphism Ψ gives a nonconstant U→Z(p) when j(E) is nonconstant; its multiplier determines the component.

proofRoute: Choose frames étale-locally, transport by Ψ, descend the invariant quotient map and extend to the proper base.
acceptance: Ψ and −Ψ define the same coarse map but Ψ must remain available as linear input.

targetCoverage.title: Descent from projective congruence to an actual isogeny

source.locator: Reduction of Theorems 1–2 to Theorem 3, p.710
source.match: Hecke containment yields a geometric cyclic isogeny f with f[p]=λΨ; rank-one geometric Hom implies σf=±f, and actual Ψ forces the plus sign for odd p.

proofRoute: Lift the generic point through the cyclic correspondence, descend the morphism using its invertible torsion restriction, then extend over U by the imported Néron interface.
acceptance: Full SL₂ monodromy is not an assumption of this descent; projective data alone permit a quadratic twist.

targetCoverage.title: Algebraically closed characteristic-zero reduction

source.locator: Theorems 1–3, p.710; proof carried out over C in §§2–7
source.match: The same complex rigidity threshold works over any algebraically closed characteristic-zero k.

proofRoute: Descend the map and a pencil of degree <N to a finitely generated subfield, embed that field in C, descend Hecke containment faithfully flatly and lift the generic isogeny over k.
acceptance: An embedding of all of k into C is not asserted.

targetCoverage.title: Abramovich linear modular gonality

source.locator: ABR96, Theorem 0.1 and §§1.4–1.7, preprint pp.1–3; BT16 remark after Theorem 2, p.710
source.match: A congruence subgroup of PSL₂(Z) of index D has compact modular curve gonality ≥7D/800.

proofRoute: Combine the imported gap 21/100, effective area πD/3 and singular-metric Li–Yau bound λ′₁Area≤8πgon.
acceptance: The exact scalar product (21/100)/24 is 7/800; arbitrary noncongruence subgroups are excluded.

targetCoverage.title: Full torsion monodromy for bounded gonality

source.match: Bounded-gonality nonisotrivial elliptic families have full actual SL₂(F_p) image for p>max(5,800N/7), also over general algebraically closed characteristic-zero k.

proofRoute: A coset action of index
acceptance: A full projective image still requires exclusion of a proper subgroup above it; no semisimplification replaces actual image.

targetCoverage.title: Bounded-genus rigidity

source.match: For genus g<N the nonconstant image is Hecke after enlarging the geometric threshold to M_(N+1).

proofRoute: Use gon≤g+1≤N<N+1; handle constant maps separately.
acceptance: A bound stated for strict gonality <N cannot be applied directly at gon=N.

targetCoverage.title: Rational and elliptic curves are Hecke

source.match: For p>M_3, every integral rational or elliptic curve in Z(p) is Hecke.

proofRoute: Apply rigidity to its normalization, of gonality one or two, and identify equal-dimensional integral images.
acceptance: The normalization genus is used even for a singular image curve.

targetCoverage.title: Cyclic quotient singularities of Z(p)

source.match: Resolve the cyclic quotient points with effective orders 2,3,p and tangent weights of type 1/n(1,a); known curves are exceptional components and Hecke strict transforms.

proofRoute: Apply the separate Hirzebruch–Jung surface supplier to the local stabilizer characters.
acceptance: The 1/2(1,1) chart gives one (−2)-curve, which cannot be contracted to a smooth point by the (−1) criterion.

targetCoverage.title: Known-curve minimal model

source.match: For sufficiently large p some smooth minimal model is reached by contractions whose original strict transforms are known rational curves.

proofRoute: Classify rational curves on the resolution, then apply Castelnuovo and Picard-number termination from the surface owner.
acceptance: A curve contracted later need not have self-intersection −1 on the initial resolution; uniqueness is not claimed.

targetCoverage.title: Branch locus of the diagonal quotient

source.match: The nonfree diagonal-quotient locus is exactly CM⁺∪CM⁻∪SBC, with orders 2 over j=1728, 3 over j=0, and p at SBC.

proofRoute: Use the individual effective inertia list and coprimality to exclude mixed types.
acceptance: A cusp/elliptic pair has no common nonidentity inertia when p>3.

targetCoverage.title: CM± coset criterion

source.match: The Heegner centralizer argument uses the identity normalizer coset; the other CM sign is obtained through conjugation rather than a chosen integral normalizer lift.

proofRoute: Read the corrected h₀=1 proof and the Gaussian/Eisenstein rank argument with the two characteristic polynomials distinguished.
acceptance: A common integral lift in the other normalizer coset is not assumed to exist.

targetCoverage.title: Hecke divisors and non-Hecke curves on Z(p)

source.locator: §1, p.709; Theorem 3 p.710; used in Theorem 29 and Propositions 25–26, erratum Propositions 4.1–4.2
source.match: A Hecke curve is an irreducible component of the finite image H_m of the cyclic prime-to-p correspondence T_m.

proofRoute: Import the parent's compactified cyclic correspondence and degree ψ(m); add only its quotient image and the non-Hecke component condition.
acceptance: At m=4 the cyclic multiplier is 6, while the full-subgroup multiplier is 7.

targetCoverage.title: Hecke curves contain no anti-Heegner CM points

source.locator: Remark 16, first clause, p.727; used in erratum §1
source.match: An ordinary cyclic prime-to-p Hecke locus has no CM⁻ point.

proofRoute: In the commutative CM endomorphism algebra the isogeny intertwines the same tangent character; prime-to-p torsion distinguishes the opposite one.
acceptance: This exclusion does not imply unconditional repulsion among anti-Heegner points.

targetCoverage.title: The maps i_p, γ_p and q_p for X(p)

source.locator: BT16 opening of §3 and Lemma 5, pp.717–718; accepted filling-witness correction
source.match: The compact triangle map γ_p kills the normal closure of the peripheral pth power; Ξ(p) is the image of Γ(p) and its quotient deck group is PSL₂(F_p).

proofRoute: Compare the cusped and filled orbifold groups and use the accepted nontrivial compact witness where an upper systolic bound is needed.
acceptance: The element U(p)L(−p) lies in the filling kernel despite being cusped hyperbolic.

targetCoverage.title: Z(p) is of general type for p > 11 (Hermann)

source.locator: §1, p.710; used for uniqueness of the minimal model in Corollary 32, p.742
source.match: The general-type and uniqueness assertion is outside this route's retained mathematical targets.

proofRoute: Follow the owner's explicit exclusion: minimal-model existence follows from known rational curves and contractions without Hermann's classification.
acceptance: No theorem for p>11 or uniqueness is inferred; the excluded statement is not marked proved or imported.

requests.need: Relative point-ball volume comparison: for n≥1, a closed effective analytic one-cycle C in Dⁿ, the sum curvature −1 area, max-product balls about zero, and 1≤r≤R−2, prove V_C(r)≤C_n(1+r)exp(r−R)V_C(R), where C_n depends only on n. For a compact quotient require R<ρ_X and lift the ball. This is additional to the existing point-multiplicity lower bound, not a consequence of the diagonal-tube theorem. On the normalization put u=log max_i|z_i|², s_t=log tanh²(t/2), h(s)=−log(1−exp(s)), v=Σ_i h(log|z_i|²), and N(s)=∫_{u<s}dd^c u. Green identity gives ∫(b−u)dd^c v+∫v dd^c u=∫_{u=b}v d^c u, hence V(r)/(4π)≤n h(s_(r+1))N(s_(r+1))/(s_(r+1)−s_r). On each active-coordinate region, ω≥4π h″(u)du∧d^c u. Coarea gives V(R)/(4π)≥[h′(s_R)−h′(s_(R−1))]N(s_(R−1)). Monotonicity of N and elementary exponential bounds prove the assertion. Prove regular-level formulas first and pass to open sublevels by left limits, including cycle weights and branches. Checks: the coordinate fibre has V(t)=4π sinh²(t/2); zero cycles and weights behave additively; the line w=az, 0<a<1, shows V(t)/a(t) decreases and must not be specified as increasing. This review checked the derivation step by step; ownership remains HV.4.

For any nonconstant finite map of smooth proper connected algebraic curves B→D over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, gon(D)≤gon(B). Proof: push a pencil’s fibre divisors to D, use the norm of ratios for linear equivalence, show the family varies, remove base points and take a pencil of degree at most the original. No existing HV.6 node states this domination lemma.

Elementary trigonometry of the curvature −1 half-plane, which the upstream FuchsianOrbifolds roadmap does not state: a hyperbolic element of PSL₂(R) with |tr|>2 has translation length 2arcosh(|tr|/2), attained on its axis; the second law of cosines for a geodesic triangle with angles α,β,γ; and, for a rotation by angle θ about a point at distance d, the displacement D satisfies sinh(D/2)=sinh d·|sin(θ/2)|.

Projective finite quotients and the cycle morphism. The atlas node SF.1/finite-group-quotient gives the scheme quotient, its orbit fibres and universal property; the upstream SchemeAndStackFoundations README §1.17 (finiteGroupQuotient_projective) states projectivity of Y/Γ for Y projective over a Noetherian base, with the invariant norm polarization M=⊗γ*L and flat base change, but no atlas node states it yet. In the named setting of projective characteristic-zero surfaces: resolve cyclic quotient charts 1/n(1,a), with Hirzebruch–Jung chains, rational exceptional components and strict transforms; provide Castelnuovo contraction of smooth rational (−1)-curves to smooth projective surfaces and termination by decreasing Picard number.
